learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Exit misses may release one bounded function-specific repair and one fresh re-entry.

items.title: Starting check: identify a belief
items.prompt: A person says, “Reusable bottles reduce plastic waste.” Which attitude component is expressed most directly?
options: Affective component
Cognitive component
Behavioral component
Situational constraint
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: identify a feeling
items.prompt: A patient says, “I feel anxious whenever I think about dental visits.” Which component is most direct?
options: Cognitive component
Behavioral component
External opportunity
Affective component
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: locate an intention
items.prompt: A voter says, “I intend to attend the local forum next week.” Which attitude component is represented?
options: Behavioral component
Cognitive component
Affective component
Measurement error
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: find the mismatch
items.prompt: Mara believes cycling is efficient and says she enjoys it, but she intends to drive every day. Which description is best?
options: All three components are negative
Only the cognitive component is present
Positive belief and feeling conflict with the plan
The behavior is guaranteed to change the belief
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: classify and align
items.prompt: Jon says a food is nutritious, feels disgust when smelling it, and plans to avoid it. Which interpretation best preserves all three observations?
options: The attitude is uniformly favorable across all components
Positive belief conflicts with negative feeling and avoidance
The smell reaction is cognitive and the nutrition claim is affective
The avoidance intention proves the nutrition belief is false
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: alter one component
items.prompt: A learner initially believes a class is useful, enjoys it, and plans to enroll again. After one event, enjoyment becomes dislike while the belief and plan remain favorable. What changes most directly?
options: The cognitive component becomes unfavorable
The behavioral component disappears
All attitude components remain aligned
The attitude becomes less internally aligned
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: classify before evaluating
items.prompt: Which statement is behavioral attitude evidence rather than a belief or feeling?
options: “I will volunteer at the shelter on Saturday.”
“The shelter improves animal welfare.”
“I feel hopeful when I visit the shelter.”
“The shelter is located two blocks away.”
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: inspect a new pattern
items.prompt: Lina believes a museum is valuable, feels excited about visiting, and buys a ticket. How are the components arranged?
options: Cognitive evidence is absent
Affect conflicts with the other components
All three components align favorably
The ticket purchase proves context never matters
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: compare before and after
items.prompt: Two components remain favorable, while the third changes from favorable to unfavorable. What is the most direct structural result?
options: The three components become more aligned
Mismatch among the components increases
The attitude can no longer contain any cognitive evidence
Behavior becomes certain in one direction
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: move the selective change
items.prompt: A person dislikes public speaking and expects it to go poorly, but begins volunteering for presentations. Which update is most precise?
options: Affect and cognition immediately become favorable
The behavioral component is absent
All three components now point negatively
Behavior conflicts with the negative belief and feeling
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Starting check: locate inconsistency
items.prompt: Which case most directly contains behavior-attitude inconsistency that could produce cognitive dissonance?
options: A person enjoys running and chooses to run
A person dislikes taxes and complains about them
A waste opponent knowingly discards recyclables
A person has no opinion about a film and has not seen it
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: follow the requests
items.prompt: A resident first agrees to place a small recycling sticker in a window and later agrees to organize a neighborhood drive. Which process best fits?
options: Foot-in-the-door
Role-playing
Classical conditioning
Attitude measurement
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: identify enacted role
items.prompt: Participants repeatedly act as peer counselors in structured sessions and later report more favorable views of counseling. Which process is most directly illustrated?
options: Foot-in-the-door
Dissonance from weak payment
Simple attitude observation
Role-playing
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: reduce dissonance
items.prompt: A student values honesty but submits copied work and cannot undo the submission. Which response would most directly reduce inconsistency by changing attitude?
options: Increase the importance of honesty even further
Decide that this copying was not very wrong
Repeat the copied submission immediately
Forget that the assignment existed
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: use external justification
items.prompt: A participant freely argues against an initial position and receives only a trivial reward. Which later result best fits dissonance reduction through attitude change?
options: The initial attitude becomes more extreme with no reconciliation
The participant concludes that the trivial reward fully forced the behavior
The participant shifts somewhat toward the argued position
The participant necessarily forgets the initial position
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: identify the sequence
items.prompt: A campaign first asks visitors to click a one-question pledge and later asks the same visitors to complete a related hour-long volunteer shift. Which process is targeted?
options: Foot-in-the-door
Role-playing
Cognitive dissonance from low reward
Deterministic attitude control
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: locate the reduction
items.prompt: A person performs a counterattitudinal act with little external pressure. Which change would reduce the resulting inconsistency?
options: Make the original attitude and behavior even more opposed
Remove every situational fact from memory
Add a second unrelated attitude conflict
Shift the attitude toward the performed behavior
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: apply weak justification
items.prompt: A volunteer publicly supports a policy they initially oppose and receives no meaningful reward. Which later shift is most consistent with attitude-based dissonance reduction?
options: A stronger rejection of the policy solely because no reward was offered
A modestly more favorable private attitude toward the policy
Complete certainty that context never affects attitudes
Loss of all memory for the public statement
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: map the process cue
items.prompt: Which sequence is necessary for a foot-in-the-door interpretation?
options: A strong attitude followed by one matching action
An assigned role followed by reflection on the role
A small request, then a larger related request
Counterattitudinal behavior followed by discomfort
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: classify enacted behavior
items.prompt: Students spend a semester enacting legislative roles in simulations and later report changed views of lawmaking. Which process best fits the sequence?
options: Role-playing
Foot-in-the-door
Dissonance from trivial payment
Attitude-guided behavior only
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Starting check: match specificity
items.prompt: Which attitude is most closely matched to predicting whether a student will attend a campus flu clinic tomorrow at noon?
options: A general attitude toward modern medicine
A general belief that health matters
An attitude toward campus buildings
An attitude toward attending that clinic tomorrow
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: identify the barrier
items.prompt: Rae strongly favors donating blood and intends to donate today, but the only center closes before Rae leaves work. What most directly disrupts the attitude-behavior link?
options: The favorable attitude lacks any direction
A situational opportunity constraint
A role-playing process
A cognitive component mismatch
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: strengthen accessibility
items.prompt: Which change would most plausibly make an attitude more available when a matching action is chosen?
options: Make the attitude less specific and harder to recall
Add an unrelated situational barrier
Recent direct experience with the attitude object
Measure a different attitude object entirely
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: locate another determinant
items.prompt: A worker favors taking public transit but drives because the night shift ends after transit service stops. Which factor best explains the behavior?
options: Available transportation opportunity
A necessarily negative transit attitude
Foot-in-the-door compliance
Affective-cognitive alignment alone
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: compare opportunity
items.prompt: Two people report equally strong favorable attitudes toward composting. Only Person B has access to a collection bin. Which bounded prediction is best?
options: Both people are certain to compost
Neither person can compost because attitudes never guide behavior
Person A is more likely because lacking a bin strengthens intention
Person B is more likely to compost because the opportunity is available
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: remove a barrier
items.prompt: Employees’ favorable attitudes toward cycling remain stable. A workplace adds secure bicycle storage, removing a major theft concern. What should increase most directly?
options: The certainty that every employee will cycle
More attitude-consistent cycling
The need to infer attitudes solely from behavior
The cognitive dissonance caused by weak rewards
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: compare matched cases
items.prompt: Which person is more likely to perform a behavior when all else stated is equal?
options: A person with a broad unrelated attitude and no opportunity
A person with a weak inaccessible attitude and a strong barrier
A person with a strong specific attitude and a clear opportunity
A person whose behavior is declared certain from attitude alone
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: compare a new behavior
items.prompt: Who is more likely to attend a lecture, based only on the supplied information?
options: A ticket holder with free time and a favorable lecture attitude
A person with a broad interest in learning but no ticket
A person with no stated attitude and a scheduling conflict
A person said to be certain to attend from attitude alone
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: isolate the context change
items.prompt: Attitude strength is held constant while a major barrier is removed. Which conclusion is most defensible?
options: The attitude itself necessarily becomes stronger
Behavior becomes unrelated to the attitude
Every person must perform the behavior
Attitude-consistent behavior becomes more likely
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: change a social norm
items.prompt: A student’s favorable attitude toward asking questions remains unchanged, but a new classroom norm openly rewards questions. What is the best prediction?
options: The favorable attitude must disappear
Attitude-consistent question asking becomes more likely
Question asking becomes impossible despite the supportive norm
Every student will ask the same number of questions
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.
